lead.title: Burnt out cars and shattered glass on Paris streets after protests turn to riots and looting
lead.note: Parisians woke to burnt out cars and shattered glass after protests in France turned into riots and looting. According to the report, around 1,800 people were arrested after nationwide protests saw outbreaks of violence and vandalism. That figure is higher than the arrest totals reported earlier in the week, so the scale of the unrest has grown. The images from the Paris streets show the damage left behind once the crowds had gone. For a reader following world news, this is the main development in France today, and it sits on top of days of tension that have already filled the front page. The number of arrests and the extent of the damage will likely shape what officials say next. Check the coverage later in the day for any further detail on the aftermath and the response.

In Southern California, hot winds drove a fire that burned coastal homes.

In Georgia, nearly 189,000 people voted on the first day of early voting. That beat the 2022 first day by more than 50,000. Ossoff and Collins clashed in a Senate debate. The regional commission released 10 housing actions, and the proposed Zoning 2.0 code drew criticism. The Atlanta Dream reached the WNBA Finals, with Games 3 and 4 at State Farm Arena.
